t: You are in St George's Square, a very long garden square in Pimlico. Gardens and a church sit in its central stretch, and Lupus Street cuts across near the northern, narrow end. Grosvenor Road runs along the southern side, with a small public garden in front of the Thames. Pimlico tube station is a short walk east. The square takes its name from Saint George, the early Christian martyr and soldier. Bram Stoker, author of Dracula, died here. So did Henry Selfe, a barrister who helped found the Canterbury settlement in New Zealand. Zoë Fairfield, of the Student Christian Movement, was born here.
